question: Veer has ₹1617 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Nitin and Pravin and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Nitin and Pravin got same amount after 16 and 17 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Veer give to Nitin?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of shares of Nitin and Pravin = (1 + 10/100)¹⁷ − ¹⁶ : 1 = 11 : 10

Total ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts ≡ ₹1617

Value of 1 part = 1617 ÷ 21 = ₹77

Nitin's share = 11 × 77 = ₹847

**∴ The correct answer is ₹847.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount Veer has = ₹1617

Rate of interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

Time for Nitin (T₁) = 16 years, Time for Pravin (T₂) = 17 years

 
 
 

 
 

 
 Total = ₹1617

 

 

 
 Nitin (N)

 
 Pravin (P)

 
• 
 
• 

 16 yrs @ 10%
 17 yrs @ 10%

 
 Same Amount (A)

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Amount, A = P(1 + R/100)T

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Nitin's share be N and Pravin's share be P.

⇒ Total Amount = N + P = 1617

⇒ Amount received by Nitin = Amount received by Pravin

⇒ N × (1 + 10/100)¹⁶ = P × (1 + 10/100)¹⁷

⇒ N = P × (1 + 10/100)¹⁷ − ¹⁶

⇒ N/P = (110/100)¹ = 11/10

⇒ Nitin's share = (11 / 21) × 1617

⇒ Nitin's share = 11 × 77 = ₹847

**∴ The correct answer is ₹847.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount after T years with principal P and rate R% compounded annually is given by A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Shares for Same Final Amount

If sums P₁ and P₂ are invested at R% such that their final amounts are equal after T₁ and T₂ years respectively, then their principal ratio follows P₁/P₂ = (1 + R/100)T² − T¹.
